correctness.rationale: A parking word has t_i=#{letters<=i}>=i for all i. Group its unique weakly increasing runs as a run-by-letter multiplicity array, ordered by weakly increasing run minima. The transfer state (placed copies t, opened runs k, set S of earlier boundaries whose strict descent has been witnessed) encodes exactly these conditions. A new letter opens h nonempty runs and fulfills q old boundaries; stars-and-bars gives C(a+b,b+q+h) for k>=1, or C(a-1,h-1) when k=0. Newly opened boundaries remain unsatisfied until a later higher letter enters the preceding run. Each completed state corresponds bijectively to one flattened parking word; nonfinal runs have length>=2 so r<=ceil(n/2). Independent literal enumeration n=1..6 matched the claimed rows; infinite n follows from the bijection, not tests.

value.rationale: The 2022/2023 paper explicitly asks for an unrestricted enumeration refined by weakly increasing run count and only gives data through n=8. This binomial-transfer algorithm resolves that natural stated problem for every n and every allowable r, with nonnegative explicit integer coefficients. It neither claims a small fixed-order scalar recurrence nor novelty of the original flattened notion.

scientific_limitations: Integer n>=1; full run count but not a fixed-state automaton independent of n.
Finite checks through n=6 by literal definition do not prove the recurrence for unbounded n.
